one_liner: Evidence-backed emergency cash planner: contract clauses become reviewed rules, a dependency graph and a CP-SAT action schedule, then the saved plan is exhaustively verified against declared uncertainty bounds with concrete counterexamples.
problem: People facing an income interruption must juggle rent, bills, approved payment shifts and cancellation clauses to avoid going negative; existing tools don't reason over interacting clauses or prove a plan survives an uncertain payday.
target_user: Individuals bridging a short cash-timing gap (e.g., final paycheck delayed) who hold contracts/bills with deferral, cancellation or assistance clauses.
core_loop: Upload doc -> native text (or consented Nemotron OCR) -> Nemotron Lightning extracts typed rule/action candidates with quote spans -> deterministic validator checks quotes/offsets/amounts/dates literally in source -> Nemotron Omni evidence check -> human review + approval gates -> CP-SAT plans action schedule maximizing minimum cash -> Recharts projection + decision trace -> user declares uncertainty bounds -> exhaustive finite-state verification returns SAFE/UNSAFE/UNKNOWN with counterexample -> cash-gap minimality diagnostic -> resilient schedule search + fingerprinted adoption.
mocked_or_hardcoded: Demo path is fully fixture-backed: the six synthetic docs' rules, events and actions are hand-coded in backend/clausegraph/demo.py (no model extracts them); demo script explicitly makes zero model calls. Real upload->worker->Nemotron path is implemented (httpx adapters, JSON-schema output, literal validators) but per the team's own EXTRACTION_CHECK.md both hosted NVIDIA attempts FAILED (native text timeout at 120s; OCR HTTP 503); the only successful live extraction was on a self-hosted Brev H100 via SSH tunnel (3/5 then 5/5 exact fields on five synthetic clauses). scripts/eval_nemotron.py default mode scores fixture candidates through local gates, not the model. Consequence walkthrough is a null placeholder component. ElevenLabs STT/TTS, Gemini, Tiger Data, DO Spaces adapters exist but were never live-tested. Resilient synthesis needs a separate 3-doc fixture because the main fixture admits no resilient schedule.
demo_risks: Low for the synthetic story (local SQLite, no network, prepared fallback runbook, reset script). High for any live extraction: hosted NVIDIA endpoints timed out/503'd; Brev GPU must be running with tunnel; 120s provider timeout. Rehearsal log says no human spoken run was ever recorded; only a 180s Playwright-driven run. UI is dense and caveat-heavy, easy to lose a judge in 3 minutes.
ui_experience: Polished SaaS dashboard: dark sidebar, 3 metric cards, 4 tabs (overview/documents/graph/history), Recharts step chart with baseline/plan lines and a red dashed counterexample overlay, React Flow dependency graph with click-to-evidence and rule highlighting, Radix evidence drawer with blockquoted source, review queue, scenario side-by-side previews, Verify panel with presets, cash-gap and resilient-plan panels, upload/consent/audio/settings dialogs. ~20 components, 13 media queries, responsive to 390px, focus management. Small 13px/9px type, long explanatory prose, no motion beyond spinners.
integrity_flags: All 48 commits fall inside the window (Sep 19 12:21 to Sep 20 10:56 EDT); no secrets committed (.env gitignored). However commit b547df2 at 13:38 on Sep 19 (2h38m after start) already dropped ~4.7K lines of working backend/frontend/tests/CI/Docker/migrations/deploy template plus AGENTS.md and handoff docs; consistent with heavy Codex-agent generation rather than a starter kit, but worth asking about. No copied prior-hackathon project detected.
ai_scaffolding_flags: Heavy: AGENTS.md (12KB contributor contract), CLAUDE.md, 52 handoff docs under docs/handoffs, branch names codex/dev-a and codex/dev-b, docs/decisions ADRs, and an explicit 'solo completion instruction' authorizing 'this agent' to act as orchestrator for developers A/B/C. Docs (~3.3K md lines + 2.5K generated types) are comparable to the ~7K lines of hand-written source; code style (one-line dense JSX, exhaustive caveats) reads as agent-authored.
novelty_notes: Cash-flow planners are common, but the mechanism is new: evidence-gated rule compiler that rejects any amount/date not literally quoted in the source, integer-cent CP-SAT lexicographic optimizer over clause-derived actions, exhaustive bounded model checking of a fixed schedule with counterexample witness, proven-minimal hypothetical cash diagnostic (amount passes, one cent less fails), and resilient-schedule synthesis with fingerprinted adoption. Formal verification of household finance is not something judges see often.
need_notes: Specific, plausible pain (income gap + interacting deferral/cancellation clauses) with genuine domain insight (deferral is timing not savings; cancellation accelerates existing debt; unapproved benefits cannot enter a plan). No user quotes, data or interviews; persona and documents are synthetic.
wow_moment: Declare 'payday could be any day Sep 21-28', click Verify: the $50-minimum plan flips to UNSAFE, a red counterexample line appears on the cash chart (payday Sep 27 -> -$400 on Sep 26), and one click opens the exact quoted clause. Then 'Explain cash gap' proves $400 is the minimum buffer because $399.99 fails.
score_rationale: S1 8: familiar category, genuinely new mechanism (formal verification + evidence-gated compiler). S2 6: real specific pain, domain insight, no user evidence. S3 7: strong Xtract traceability and honest Nemotron eval with documented failures, stacks with Compound, but sponsor model never runs in the demo and hosted path failed. S4 12: synthetic loop polished, 248 backend + 61 real-API browser tests, CI; live extraction unproven, walkthrough stubbed. S5 9: attractive interactive dashboard, dense text. Wow 6: one clear neat moment.
judge_summary: A contract-clause-to-cash-plan tool that formally verifies a saved payment schedule and shows the exact payday that breaks it in red on the chart. Extremely rigorous engineering and honest docs, but the whole demo runs on hand-coded synthetic fixtures; live Nemotron extraction only worked on a self-hosted GPU.
